rules.source_commentary: करोतीति कारुः , शिल्पी कारकश्च । [[7.3.33]] <<आतो युक्…>> वातीति वायुः । पायुर्गुदम् । जयत्यभिभवति रोगान् जायुरौषधम् । मिनोति प्रक्षिपति देहे ऊष्माणमिति मायुः पित्तम् । स्वादुः । साध्नोति परकार्यं साधुः । अश्नुते आशु शीघ्रम् । आशुर्व्रीहिः पाटलः स्यात् ।
rules.decision: The final marker ṇ is lost in the word. It remains available to the applicable vṛddhi rule. With vā, the ā-final stem takes yuk before the vowel-initial marked suffix under 7.3.33. The eight listed stems have separate lexical inputs and glosses.

inputs.sense: the anus, in the source gloss
bile, described through heat in the body
swiftly, or the variety of rice specified in the commentary

rules.decision: Inherit uṇ. Replace the 1.1 root list by iṇ and require chandas. The source gives an oblique word āyau, not a nominative citation. Ṛgveda 1.114.8a witnesses that inflection.

inputs.sense: the lexical stem recovered from the locative āyau

rules.source_commentary: दीर्यत इति दारु । स्नुः प्रस्थः सानुरस्त्रियाम् । जानु । जानुनी । इह [[7.3.35]] <<जनिवध्योश्च>> इति न निषेधः । अनुबन्धद्वयसामर्थ्यात् । चारु रम्यम् । चाटु प्रियं वाक्यम् । मृगय्वादित्वात्कुप्रत्यये चटु इत्यपि ।
rules.decision: Initial ñ and final ṇ are separate it markers. The commentary explicitly attributes jānu to the force of both markers despite 7.3.35. Its short-a caṭu belongs to a distinct ku derivation and has no ñuṇ reading credit.

rules.source_commentary: किं शृणोतीति किंशारुः सस्यशूकं बाणश्च । जरामेति जरायुर्गर्भाशयः । गर्भाशयो जरायुः स्यात् ।
rules.decision: Keep the two source paraphrases paired with their respective first constituents and outcomes. They do not license the crossed pairings. The exact lexical root IDs are left unassigned where the prose does not give them.

inputs.sense: fetal covering or receptacle in the source gloss

rules.decision: Preserve the local change r to l and the instrumental sense of the paraphrase. The marked suffix has the same audible vowel as in 1.1.

rules.decision: Keep kṛka, vac, the specified k change and the ñuṇ history. The lexical senses quoted from Viśva belong to the resulting word.
